import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import io

# Prepare the data from the string
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and modern style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")
plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-poster")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create a bubble chart to show multiple dimensions
# x-axis: Megapixels
# y-axis: Price
# bubble size: Max ISO (a key performance metric)
# bubble color: Brand
# marker style: Body Type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='max_iso',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Emphasize the difference in ISO
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor='black',
    alpha=0.8,
    linewidth=1.5
)

# --- Customize the plot for clarity and impact ---

# Set titles and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Analysis: Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=28, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=20, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=20, labelpad=15)

# Format y-axis ticks as currency for readability
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(fontsize=14)
plt.yticks(fontsize=14)

# Annotate each point with its model year and weight for extra context
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['megapixels'],
        row['price_usd'] + 150,  # Offset text slightly above the point
        f"{row['model_year']}\n{row['weight_grams']}g",
        ha='center',
        va='bottom',
        fontsize=12,
        color='black',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc='aliceblue', ec='grey', lw=1, alpha=0.8)
    )

# Improve the legend by placing it outside the plot
ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0., title_fontsize='16', fontsize='14')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the final visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
